questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country and the Canadian nature is beautiful.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of different websites and it was a bit difficult navigating in the beginning but I managed. 
There is a very good and helpful student counselor for international students, who returned emails within a day. That helped a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I only arrived a couple of days before school started so most of the help I received was from friends.
I did go to a couple of orientation events, but those were useless for international students, so if I could do it over, I would not spend money on the O week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of Facebook groups (UWO off campus housing) and you can be lucky to find accommodation on Airbnb as well. It was pretty easy and we had a great landlord but our house was pretty far from campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure the distance to campus is no longer than 15-20 minutes by bus. I would also make sure to live by a bus stop with a direct connection to campus, because of constructions throughout the city, that makes it close to impossible to catch a connecting bus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You look through the course catalogue and find courses that look interesting. They have an online course builder that makes it easy for you to see if you have overlapping courses. On this website you can see the number of available spots and the hours of lecture and tutorial. When you have chosen the courses you want to apply for, you go to another website where you make the request. It takes some time before you see whether you got the courses or not (depending on the time you make the application). If you don't get the courses you want, you apply again for different courses. 
Courses have different letters depending on what kind of course it is and what time of year it is offered, so make sure to check the course letter before applying.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international student counselor was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty simple once I cracked the code and I got three courses the first time I applied. The second time I applied I got my last course. 
I wanted to drop one course and add another one within the first week of school and that was easy as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the course codes before applying for forhåndsgodkendelse. I applied for a lot of courses that is offered during the spring semester and I was there in the fall.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had 1 first year course, 1 second year course, 1 third year course, and 1 fourth year course. 
None of the courses were too difficult and some of them could have been more challenging, but that suited me fine and gave me more spare time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Only one of my courses used a book so everything we had to know for the exam was presented during lectures. 
Two of my courses were only lectures and had no tutorials. 
All courses had midterms and some also had marks for participation and assignments, so the exam did not count 100%.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biology 4355F, the biology of aging
Biology 3592A, human genetics
Microimm 2500A, biology of infection and immunology 
Psychol 1002A, psychology as a natural science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Biology 4355F is the best course I have taken during my bachelors so far. The professor was great and the topics he covered was so interesting and has opened my eyes to how interesting aging processes are.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as possible! Prioritize to see nature in the early fall and cities later on because of the weather.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I met a lot of locals when going out at night.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is very friendly and talkative and they want to help you in any way they can.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Live on campus or close by. 
2. Try to place your classes on the same days so you can go away on a long weekend. I was off thursday and friday and that made it much easier to travel. 
3. Choose interesting courses and not just easy ones. It makes it so much more fun to attend class.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't spend money on O week, it is mostly for first year students and not exchange. 
If you need cooking supplies, plates, cutlery etc. go to a thrift shop instead of buying it in stores. It is much cheaper.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Academics was great and especially the aging course.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything has been pretty easy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
